_help: Real data from the NASA Exoplanet Archive, Planetary Systems Composite Parameters (pscomppars). null = the archive has no value (shown as 'unknown'). Refresh with: python3 fetch_postcards.py
source: NASA Exoplanet Archive, Planetary Systems Composite Parameters table (pscomppars)
citation: This research has made use of the NASA Exoplanet Archive, which is operated by the California Institute of Technology, under contract with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration under the Exoplanet Exploration Program.
query: select pl_name,hostname,pl_letter,sy_snum,sy_pnum,sy_dist,pl_orbper,pl_orbsmax,pl_rade,pl_bmasse,pl_bmassprov,pl_dens,pl_eqt,pl_insol,pl_orbeccen,pl_orbincl,st_spectype,st_teff,st_rad,st_mass,st_lum,st_age,disc_year,discoverymethod,disc_facility,cb_flag,pl_controv_flag,tran_flag,ttv_flag,disc_pubdate,pl_rade_reflink,pl_bmasse_reflink,pl_eqt_reflink,pl_orbsmax_reflink,st_rad_reflink,st_teff_reflink from pscomppars where hostname in ('51 Peg','55 Cnc','GJ 1214','GJ 667 C','HD 189733','HD 209458','HD 80606','HR 8799','K2-18','KELT-9','KOI-351','Kepler-10','Kepler-16','Kepler-1649','Kepler-186','Kepler-22','Kepler-442','Kepler-452','Kepler-47','Kepler-62','LHS 1140','PSR B1257+12','Proxima Cen','Ross 128','TOI-1338 A','TOI-700','TRAPPIST-1','Teegarden''s Star','WASP-12','WASP-121','WASP-76','bet Pic') order by hostname, pl_orbper

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 b
planets.why: Innermost of seven Earth-sized worlds in a resonant chain.

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 c
planets.why: Second of seven; its year is 2.4 days.

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 d
planets.why: On the warm inner edge of the habitable zone.

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 e
planets.why: The most Earth-like of the seven by size and sunlight.

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 f
planets.why: A cool world in the habitable zone; maybe icy.

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 g
planets.why: The second-largest of the seven, in the cold outer zone.

planets.name: TRAPPIST-1 h
planets.why: The outer planet, whose period was predicted before it was measured.

planets.name: Proxima Cen b
planets.why: The closest known exoplanet: orbits the nearest star to the Sun.

planets.name: Kepler-186 f
planets.why: The first Earth-sized planet found in a star's habitable zone.

planets.name: Kepler-452 b
planets.why: 'Earth's cousin': a near-year orbit around a Sun-like star.

planets.name: TOI-700 d
planets.why: An Earth-sized habitable-zone world found by TESS.

planets.name: LHS 1140 b
planets.why: A dense super-Earth in the habitable zone of a nearby red dwarf.

planets.name: K2-18 b
planets.why: A sub-Neptune in the habitable zone; JWST saw methane and CO2 in its air.

planets.name: Teegarden's Star b
planets.why: One of the most Earth-like planets known, around a tiny nearby star.

planets.name: Ross 128 b
planets.why: A temperate world around a quiet red dwarf only 11 light-years away.

planets.name: Kepler-442 b
planets.why: A super-Earth in its star's habitable zone.

planets.name: Kepler-62 f
planets.why: A habitable-zone super-Earth in a five-planet system.

planets.name: Kepler-22 b
planets.why: Kepler's first habitable-zone planet (2011).

planets.name: Kepler-1649 c
planets.why: Earth-sized, found years later hiding in old Kepler data.

planets.name: GJ 667 C c
planets.why: In a triple-star system: two more suns far off in its sky.

planets.name: Kepler-16 b
planets.why: The real 'Tatooine': a planet that orbits two suns.

planets.name: TOI-1338 b
planets.why: Another circumbinary world, found by a high-school intern at NASA.

planets.name: Kepler-47 c
planets.why: A circumbinary planet in its stars' habitable zone.

planets.name: 51 Peg b
planets.why: The first planet found around a Sun-like star (1995 Nobel Prize).

planets.name: HD 209458 b
planets.why: The first planet seen crossing its star, and the first with a detected atmosphere.

planets.name: HD 189733 b
planets.why: A deep-blue hot Jupiter where it may rain glass sideways.

planets.name: WASP-12 b
planets.why: A hot Jupiter being stretched and slowly eaten by its star.

planets.name: WASP-76 b
planets.why: Hot enough that iron may evaporate on the day side and rain on the night side.

planets.name: WASP-121 b
planets.why: A puffy hot Jupiter with metal clouds.

planets.name: KELT-9 b
planets.why: The hottest planet known: hotter than many stars.

planets.name: 55 Cnc e
planets.why: A lava-covered super-Earth whose year lasts less than a day.

planets.name: Kepler-10 b
planets.why: Kepler's first confirmed rocky planet, a scorched lava world.

planets.name: GJ 1214 b
planets.why: A hazy 'water world' candidate around a small red star.

planets.name: HD 80606 b
planets.why: On a wildly stretched orbit: heats by hundreds of degrees in hours.

planets.name: KOI-351 h
planets.why: Kepler-90 h: the outer giant in an eight-planet system, as many planets as ours.

planets.name: PSR B1257+12 c
planets.why: One of the first exoplanets ever found, orbiting a dead star (a pulsar).

planets.name: bet Pic b
planets.why: A young giant planet photographed directly.

planets.name: HR 8799 e
planets.why: One of four giant planets photographed around a young star.
